title: Conditional Automation and Operational Continuity: A Framework for Preserving Human Capacity in AI-Dependent Essential Services
content: As nations expand automation in essential services, they face a structural risk: the human operational capacity that automation displaces may not be recoverable when AI systems fail, lose connectivity, or produce unsafe outputs. Existing governance approaches address model risk and trustworthiness but do not systematically require that organizations demonstrate independent operating capability before critical automation expands. We propose the \NHACF{} (NHACF), a conceptual design framework that makes AI deployment conditional on verified human competence and tested fallback capacity. The NHACF couples task-level skill development, periodic unaided assessment, independent fallback infrastructure, and an explicit deployment gate: an organization may expand or renew critical automation only when it can demonstrate both maintained competence and sufficient independent coverage under mandated outage scenarios. Workers participate as practitioners, evaluators, mentors, and recovery operatives rather than nominal supervisors. We formalize the continuity constraint, the deployment gate condition, and the resource allocation requirements. A five-year national adoption pathway specifies governance, financing, accountability, and evaluation obligations. The framework is conceptual; its effectiveness requires empirical validation through sector pilots measuring independently assessed unaided performance, fallback coverage, and transition latency. The core policy principle is straightforward: essential-service automation should expand only with evidence that the service can continue when the primary AI capability is unavailable.
